data.title: Activist investor calls for departure of Accor CEO - FT
data.description:
An activist investor is calling for Accor (ACRFF) (ACCYY) CEO to step down days after the French hotel operator announced a deal to take control of hotel group Ennismore for €1.6 billion.

Parvus, a fund with a 14% stake worth €1.6bn in Accor, said that Sébastien Bazin, the French group’s chief executive and chair, had presided over “unfocused strategy [and] inconsistent capital allocation”, and that it would “hold the board accountable” at the next annual general meeting if it failed to take action, Parvus said in a letter seen by the Financial Times on Thursday.

The London-based activist first accumulated a stake in 2023. Accor shares have dropped 7.2% over the past two days following the Ennismore announcement. 

“In the absence of a satisfactory response or meaningful action, we now consider it necessary to seek changes to the composition of the board and management,” Parvus wrote in the letter.

Accor did not immediately reply to a request for comment from the FT.

data.title: Gap cuts full-year outlook, brings in Vuori, Fabletics exec to run Athleta
data.description:
The Gap (GAP) reported mixed results for the third quarter, gaining market share and beating expectations for comparable store sales for its Old Navy and Gap banners.

But challenges persisted for its Athleta and Banana Republic banners, both of which saw comparable store sales decline by 15% and 3%, respectively, worse than expectations for a decline of 11% and increase of 2.45%, respectively.

“While demand softened in October and early November, amidst warmer weather, we are encouraged by the more recent improvement in trends as temperatures have cooled. As we move through the holiday season, we remain focused on delivering compelling product assortments and culturally relevant marketing across our brands, supported by a strong value proposition for our customers,” Gap CEO Richard Dickson said in a press release announcing the company’s results.

The results also reflected a 39% improvement in GAAP of $0.86, beating expectations by 9 cents thanks to IEEPA tariff refunds. The refund helped Gap’s (GAP) bottom line in light of a very modest increase in net sales. On an adjusted basis, Gap earned a profit of $0.82 per share, 4 cents better than expected.

The IEEPA refund also drove a 50-basis-point increase in operating margin to 9.9% (beating 9.34% estimates) and a 10-basis-point gain in gross margin to 42.5% (missing 43% estimates).

The full-year outlook factors in quarter-to-date performance as well as a slower than expected start to the fourth quarter. This assumes adjusted earnings to be between $2.29 and $2.34 per share, down from an earlier range of $2.35 and $2.45 and below the $2.40 consensus estimate.

Net sales for the year are now expected to be flat at $15.4B versus an earlier outlook for an increase of 1% to 1.5% and less than $15.53B estimates.

The retailer also lowered its estimate for adjusted gross margin to down slightly year-over-year from up slightly and sees an adjusted operating margin of 7.2% from a range of 7.4% and 7.6% previously.

Despite the mixed results and lowered guidance, shares are gaining ground in after-hours trading as the revision to FY26 was not as bad as expected given the continued headwinds from Athleta and Banana Republic.

The company also announced a new president and CEO for the Athleta banner. Ashley Kechter was previously global president of Vuori and Fabletics, bringing “deep activewear expertise, exceptional product instincts, and the operational rigor required to move Athleta forward.”  Kechter takes over the helm of Athleta on December 14.

data.title: Webull Q3 earnings beat, helped by strong engagement from active traders
data.description:
Webull (BULL) stock gained 0.4% in Thursday after-hours trading after the digital investment platform's Q3 earnings and revenue topped the Wall Street consensus estimates.

Q3 adjusted operating EPS of $0.13,  beating  the average analyst estimate of $0.07, rose from $0.07 in last year's Q3.

Webull (BULL) Group President and U.S. CEO Anthony Anthony Denier highlighted the company's expanding client assets and sustained trading activity. "We continued to see strong engagement among active traders, particularly in options, while advancing key initiatives across AI, futures, and international expansion," he said.

The company's Q3 revenue reached a record $218.7M, topping the $215.6M consensus and growing 39% Y/Y and 10% Q/Q.

Total operating expenses of $172.3M, just under the Visible Alpha consensus of $172.7M, increased 30% Y/Y. The growth was driven by higher brokerage and transaction costs on increased trading activity, higher share-based compensation expense, and a non-cash remeasurement loss on contingent consideration related to its Pi Securities acquisition.

Adjusted operating expenses of $146.8M climbed 24% Y/Y

Customer assets under management totaled $32.4B, up 53% Y/Y, driven by net deposits and the acquisition of Pi Securities.

Registered users rose 12% Y/Y to 29M, while funded accounts increased 5% Y/Y to 5.18M.

Daily average revenue trades jumped 66% Y/Y to 1.8M.

Revenue details:

  • Equity and option order flow rebates of $124.9M increased from $83.7M a year ago.
  • Interest-related income of $43.1M edged down from $43.4M in the year-ago quarter.
  • Handling charge income climbed to $39.8M from $23.3M.

Conference call at 5:00 PM ET.

data.title: Hallador Energy wins Indiana regulatory OK for 12-year capacity sale expected to generate $1B
data.description:
Hallador Energy (HNRG) rose 3.6% post-market Thursday after saying the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission approved a 12-year capacity agreement with an unnamed utility company, satisfying the regulatory approval condition to the agreement, which is now effective.

Hallador (HNRG) said the deal is expected to generate more than $1B in capacity revenue from its Merom Generating Station through mid-2040, at a fixed price that substantially exceeds its historical capacity pricing.

Deliveries begin with a smaller volume of accredited capacity in late 2028, rising to roughly two-thirds of Hallador's (HNRG) accredited capacity beginning in 2029 and continuing through the end of the 12-year term, the company said.

"We've put long-term contracts in place and made significant progress on our plans to grow our power business," Hallador (HNRG) President and CEO Brent Bilsland said. "This approval demonstrates that Indiana's regulators are still supporting the growth of data centers in Indiana."

data.title: Curtiss-Wright boosts 2026 buyback program by $250M
data.description:
• Curtiss-Wright (CW) announced on Thursday a $250M increase to its 2026 share repurchase program, bringing expected annual buybacks to a record $710M.

  • The company also declared a quarterly dividend of $0.26 per share, payable December 11 to shareholders of record on November 27.

  • It authorized an additional $60M in share repurchases beginning in January 2027 to offset potential dilution from employee compensation plans.

  • CEO Lynn Bamford said the expanded buyback reflects confidence in the company's financial outlook and long-term growth strategy.
